message.content: The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**, a protoplanet orbiting the young star HD 100546. It is still forming and is estimated to have a radius of about 2.5 – 3 times that of Jupiter (roughly 20–25 000 km). Because it is a protoplanet, its exact mass and radius are still being refined, but it remains the biggest planet (or planetary‑mass object) that astronomers have measured to date.
